ace.title: ACE
ace.text: Arbitrary code execution: a glitch that makes the game run instructions you write. In FireRed and LeafGreen, the instructions go in the PC box names.

glitch.title: Glitch species (0x0351)
glitch.text: A Pokémon with a species number that doesn't exist in the game. 0x0351 is the one that triggers ACE: when you pick it up in the PC, the game runs whatever is written in the box names.

mail.title: Mail glitch
mail.text: A trick with Mail, the letter a Pokémon holds: the words you pick for the message rewrite data of a Pokémon in the box. It's the first step to unlock ACE.

badegg.title: Bad Egg
badegg.text: The egg the game shows when a Pokémon's data is corrupted (the checksum doesn't match). It never hatches, but you can release it.

writer.title: Base64 writer
writer.text: An ACE setup made by Mettrich. It reads the 14 box names and writes a whole Pokémon to Box 14, slot 30: with it, a single code creates any Pokémon.

eng10.title: eng10
eng10.text: The version of the community generator's codes made for the English FireRed and LeafGreen on Switch (revision 10). The other versions are for the cartridge.

rng.title: RNG
rng.text: The game's random number generator. "Doing RNG" means acting at the right moment to get the Pokémon you want.

seed.title: Seed
seed.text: The number the generator starts from. In FireRed and LeafGreen, it depends on how long it takes you to leave the title screen.

frame.title: Frame advance
frame.text: Each roll of the random number generator since PRESS START; ten-lines and PokeFinder call it advance. Each one is a different instant to act. On menus the game rolls once per frame, about 60 per second; on the map, twice (not verified).

nature.title: Nature
nature.text: The Pokémon's personality (Adamant, Timid and others). It raises one stat by 10% and lowers another. It comes from the PID.

ivs.title: IVs
ivs.text: Values from 0 to 31 rolled when the Pokémon appears, one per stat. Higher is stronger; 31 is the maximum.

evs.title: EVs
evs.text: Points a Pokémon earns from battles and vitamins that raise its stats. Up to 255 per stat and 510 in total.

pid.title: PID
pid.text: A number rolled when the Pokémon appears. It sets nature, gender, ability and, together with the TID and SID, whether it's shiny.

ot.title: OT
ot.text: Original Trainer: the trainer who caught the Pokémon. Their name and number are stored in the Pokémon.

tid.title: TID and SID
tid.text: The trainer's numbers. The TID shows on the trainer card; the SID is secret. Together with the PID, they decide whether a Pokémon is shiny.

home.title: Pokémon HOME
home.text: Nintendo and The Pokémon Company's online service for storing Pokémon and moving them between games. Support for FireRed and LeafGreen on Switch is expected in October 2026. Don't take created or modified Pokémon there.

filter.title: Word filter
filter.text: Nintendo's list of words the Switch won't accept in names. That's why some box names used in codes get rejected.

esp32.title: ESP32
esp32.text: A cheap board with Wi-Fi. Here it works as a radio so the PC can talk to the Switch as if it were another console.

keys.title: prod.keys
keys.text: A file with a Switch's encryption keys, taken from an unlocked console. The board only uses four of them. Always use your own console's keys.

gift.title: Mystery Gift
gift.text: A game feature for receiving gifts over wireless. The ESP32 board uses it to send data to the game.

firmware.title: Firmware
firmware.text: The program that runs inside the ESP32 board.

rom.title: ROM
rom.text: The copy of the game. On Switch, it's the original Game Boy Advance ROM running in Nintendo's emulator.

title.title: Title screen
title.text: The screen with the FireRed or LeafGreen logo and the PRESS START text, right after the intro. The instant you press the button there decides the seed.

ability.title: Ability
ability.text: The Pokémon's ability, like Overgrow or Sturdy. Many species have just one; some have two, and the PID decides which one comes out: 1st or 2nd, in the game's order.

hiddenpower.title: Hidden Power
hiddenpower.text: A move almost every Pokémon learns by TM. Its type (Fire, Ice, Electric...) and power, from 30 to 70, come from the IVs, so each Pokémon has its own. It only matters if you'll use the move.

slot.title: Slot
slot.text: Which row of the map's encounter table was rolled. Grass has 12, each with a species and level; that roll decides which Pokémon shows up and how likely it is.

chance.title: Chance per attempt
chance.text: Even pressing at the right instant, the console sometimes gives a seed a few numbers off the table. This column counts in how many of those likely values the same frame advance also gives a Pokémon that passes your filters. The higher, the more attempts work.

stats.title: Stats at level
stats.text: The stats the Pokémon has at the encounter level, without EVs, as they show on the summary right after the catch (HP/Atk/Def/SpA/SpD/Spe). Use them to check in the game which frame advance you got.

pokerus.title: Pokérus
pokerus.text: A rare, helpful virus: while the Pokémon has it, it gains double EVs. In games with a clock it fades after a few days and the Pokémon becomes immune; in FR/LG, which has no clock, it never fades (the day countdown exists in the code, but the game never calls it).

fateful.title: Event (fateful encounter)
fateful.text: The event Pokémon flag. In FR/LG, Mew and Deoxys only obey with it; on a regular Pokémon it changes nothing in the game, but checkers may flag it.

ribbons.title: Ribbons
ribbons.text: The Pokémon's awards: contest ones (from Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald) and others like Champion, earned by beating the Elite Four. In FR/LG only the Champion ribbon can be earned.

ppup.title: PP Up
ppup.text: How many times that move's PP was raised with the PP Up item (or PP Max, which counts as 3). Each adds 20% of the base PP, up to 3.
